items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: Merritt and them, they did the same thing. I'd buy an instrument, they'd come along behind me and pick it up and blend it up.

ctx.x: Well, can you tell us a little bit about your brother, Henry, because he's not here, of course, to talk for us. Well, he was a hot friend. He was a wonderful, I've heard. Yes, he was. He was a showman with his son. I had that to say. How much younger was he than you? He was younger than you? Oh, yeah. Next to him. About five years. About five years. And, uh...

He'd be about 65. What's his name? Merritt and them, they did the same thing. I'd buy an instrument, they'd come along behind me and pick it up and blend it up. That's how they all went out. I'd blow a blow and essence.

How much older was Rudy than you? About... Oh, Rudy was about three or four. About five years. About five years old. Oh, you're 69? He'd be... Yeah, about five. That's right. That's right. I'm right. How old was your father when he died? Do you remember? 62, I believe. And when was that? Oh, I spent quite some time. About 10, quite some time. About 10...

items.title: Brunies Brother Band Interview, 1957-10-19
items.q: Your older brother, Richard, he was the oldest one of the years. Yeah.

ctx.x: . Now we have some time. Yeah, it's going all right now. If you can just tell us first, forget your name on Abby, so we know. Okay, this is Abby Brunus speaking. And now these folks are here wanting to know how I started. It's been so long, it's hard to remember. We're back there in 1908. When were you born? In 1900. And we started out, I think we were the first school band in the United States. There was only three pieces. And the three pieces consist of Emmett Rogers, George Brunus, and myself. And then we...…

. He played it on the floor like that and stuff. George had people stand on his chest. Yeah, jump on his chest. What we call that eccentric. So Henry did all that too. Henry done that before George did that. Yeah, sure. Henry was really the originator of it. Well, uh, start. I didn't get that on here. You say Henry could read a good reader, but the rest of you never did learn to read. No, none of us read outside of Henry. Henry would sit down and play first chair in a big 60-piece band.
